before.name: Question 1
before.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t],$ the vector space of real polynomials of degree at most $2,$ and let the inner product on $V$ be defined as

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1).
$$

Now consider the following elements of $V:$

$$
{p}_{1}(t)={t}^{2}-t,\,{p}_{2}(t)={t}^{2}+t,\,q(t)=4{t}^{2}-t-1
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $S=\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ given that ${p}_{1}(t)⊥{p}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t)}$ equals $2{t}^{2}-2t.$

decision.explanation: Since p₁ and p₂ are orthogonal, the projection onto S is the sum of the projections onto their spans. The values of p₂ at −1, 0, 1 are 0, 0, 2, while q(1)=2. Thus ⟨q,p₂⟩/⟨p₂,p₂⟩=4/4=1. Adding p₂ to the given projection gives (2t²−2t)+(t²+t)=3t²−t.

p1(t)=t2−t,p2(t)=t2+t,q(t)=4t2−t−1

Find the orthogonal projection of q(t) onto S=Span{p1(t),p2(t)} given that p1(t)⊥p2(t) with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of q(t) onto Span{p1(t)} equals 2t2−2t.

Correct
EXPLANATION

Since the set {p1(t),p2(t)} is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of q(t) onto the subspace S is given by

projSq(t)=projp1(t)q(t)+projp2(t)q(t).

We are given that projp1(t)q(t)=2t2−2t, so let's now find the orthogonal projection of q(t) onto Span{p2(t)}. This can be computed as

projp2(t)q(t)=⟨q(t),p2(t)⟩⟨p2(t),p2(t)⟩p2(t).

In our case, we have

⟨q(t),p2(t)⟩=q(−1)p2(−1)+q(0)p2(0)+q(1)p2(1)=(4t2−t−1)|−1⋅(t2+t)|−1+(4t2−t−1)|0⋅(t2+t)|0+(4t2−t−1)|1⋅(t2+t)|1=4⋅0+(−1)⋅0+2⋅2=4,

and

⟨p2(t),p2(t)⟩=p2(−1)p2(−1)+p2(0)p2(0)+p2(1)p2(1)=(t2+t)2|−1+(t2+t)2|0+(t2+t)2|1=02+02+22=4.

Therefore,

projp2(t)q(t)=44⋅(t2+t)=t2+t.

Finally,

projSq(t)=projp1(t)q(t)+projp2(t)q(t)=2t2−2t+(t2+t)=3t2−t.

Now consider the following elements of V:

f1(t)=1,f2(t)=2cos⁡t,g(t)=2sin⁡t−cos⁡t+3

Find the orthogonal projection of g(t) onto S=Span{f1(t),f2(t)} given that f1(t)⊥f2(t) with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of g(t) onto Span{f2(t)} equals −cos⁡t.

b
3−sin⁡t

cos⁡t

3−cos⁡t

decision.explanation: Because f₁ and f₂ are orthogonal, their individual projections add. The projection onto the constant function 1 is ⟨g,1⟩/⟨1,1⟩ = 6π/(2π) = 3, since both sine and cosine integrate to zero over [−π,π]. Adding the given projection −cos t gives 3−cos t.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Let $V=C[-\pi ,\pi ],$ the vector space of continuous functions over $[-\pi ,\pi ]$, and let the inner product on $V$ be defined as

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Now consider the following elements of $V:$

$$
{f}_{1}(t)=1,\,{f}_{2}(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,g(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $S=\text{Span}{{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{2}(t)}$ given that ${f}_{1}(t)⊥{f}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{f}_{2}(t)}$ equals $-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.$
after.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{2}(t)}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,g(t)={\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t).
$$

We are given that ${\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t)=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$ so let's now find the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{f}_{1}(t)}.$ This can be computed as

$$
{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)=\frac{⟨g(t),{f}_{1}(t)⟩}{⟨{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{1}(t)⟩}\,{f}_{1}(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨g(t),{f}_{1}(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }g(t){f}_{1}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3)\cdot 1\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3)\,\text{d}t \\  & =[-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+3t]_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =(2-0+3\pi )-(2-0-3\pi ) \\  & =6\pi \end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{1}(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }1\cdot 1\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }1\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t) & =\frac{6\pi }{2\pi }\cdot 1=3.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,g(t) & ={\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t) \\  & =3-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Let $V=C[-1,1],$ the vector space of continuous functions over $[-1,1]$, and let the inner product on $V$ be defined as

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-1}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Now consider the following elements of $V:$ 

$$
{f}_{1}(t)=t,\,{f}_{2}(t)={t}^{2},\,g(t)=15t+3
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $S=\text{Span}{{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{2}(t)}$ given that ${f}_{1}(t)⊥{f}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{f}_{1}(t)}$ equals $15t.$
after.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{2}(t)}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,g(t)={\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t).
$$

We are given that ${\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)=15t,$ so let's now find the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{f}_{2}(t)}.$ This can be computed as

$$
{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t)=\frac{⟨g(t),{f}_{2}(t)⟩}{⟨{f}_{2}(t),{f}_{2}(t)⟩}\,{f}_{2}(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨g(t),{f}_{2}(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}g(t){f}_{2}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(15t+3)\cdot {t}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}15{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[\frac{15}{4}{t}^{4}+{t}^{3}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{15}{4}+1)-(\frac{15}{4}-1) \\  & =2,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{f}_{2}(t),{f}_{2}(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{f}_{2}(t){f}_{2}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{t}^{2}\cdot {t}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{t}^{4}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\frac{1}{5}{t}^{5}|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}-(-\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t)=\frac{2}{(\frac{2}{5})}\cdot {t}^{2}=5{t}^{2}.
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,g(t) & ={\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t) \\  & =15t+5{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
